bill.title: Providing for consideration of the joint resolution (H.J. Res. 20) providing for congressional disapproval under chapter 8 of title 5, United States Code, of the rule submitted by the Department of Energy relating to ‘‘Energy Conservation Program: Energy Conservation Standards for Consumer Gas-fired Instantaneous Water Heaters’’; providing for consideration of the joint resolution (H.J. Res. 35) providing for congressional disapproval under chapter 8 of title 5, United States Code, of the rule submitted by the Environmental Protection Agency relating to ‘‘Waste Emissions Charge for Petroleum and Natural Gas Systems: Procedures for Facilitating Compliance, Including Netting and Exemptions’’; and providing for consideration of the concurrent resolution (H. Con. Res. 14) establishing the congressional budget for the United States Government for fiscal year 2025 and setting forth the appropriate budgetary levels for fiscal years 2026 through 2034.
bill.latestActionText: Motion to reconsider laid on the table Agreed to without objection.
bill.officialSummary: This resolution provides for the consideration of three measures. Specifically, it provides for the consideration of H.J. Res. 20, nullifying the rule submitted by the Department of Energy relating to Energy Conservation Program: Energy Conservation Standards for Consumer Gas-fired Instantaneous Water Heaters ; H.J. Res. 35, nullifying the rule submitted by the Environmental Protection Agency relating to Waste Emissions Charge for Petroleum and Natural Gas Systems: Procedures for Facilitating Compliance, Including Netting and Exemptions ; and H.Con.Res. 14, establishing the congressional budget for FY2025 and setting forth budgetary levels for FY2026 through FY2034.

classification.plainSummary: This resolution sets the procedural rules for the House to consider three separate measures. Two of those measures would nullify federal regulations—one concerning energy efficiency standards for gas water heaters and another concerning emissions charges for oil and gas facilities. The third measure would establish the federal budget framework for fiscal years 2025 through 2034.

industries.rationale: The resolution enables consideration of a measure nullifying EPA emissions charges on petroleum and natural gas systems.
The resolution enables consideration of a measure nullifying efficiency standards for consumer gas water heaters, affecting manufacturers of those appliances.
The resolution enables consideration of a measure nullifying energy conservation standards for gas-fired water heaters, which utilities may supply or regulate.

plain.whatItDoes: This resolution would provide for the consideration of three measures.
plain.whoItTouches: Nobody directly — this is about how Congress runs itself.
plain.everydayEffect: If it passed, the change would show up in nothing in an ordinary week. Nothing has changed yet. This kind of resolution does not become law, even if it passes.
plain.source: Reworded from the official summary. Staff at the Congressional Research Service wrote that summary. It is public domain, and the full text of it is further down this page.

method.formula: score = Σ_industries ( donorShare(industry) × billWeight(industry) ), where billWeight = classifierConfidence / Σ classifierConfidence. Range 0–1, read as a weighted share of disclosed itemized money.

ordinary.text: They wrote this bill. Sponsoring a bill about your own district's industry is the ordinary case, not the odd one.

disclaimer: This tool places two public records next to each other: who donated to a member of Congress, and what that member legislated on. Any overlap you see is a correlation, not causation. It is not evidence of a quid pro quo, of influence, or of wrongdoing. Legislators routinely receive support from industries in their district for the same reason they legislate on them: those industries are there.
